examples.en: I opened a cafe with a friend as partners.

examples.ko: 동업은 처음에 계약서를 잘 써야 해요.
examples.en: In a partnership, you need a good contract from the start.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 동업이 오 년 만에 끝났어요.
examples.en: The two people's partnership ended after five years.

examples.ko: 동업 상대를 고를 때는 신뢰가 제일 중요해요.
examples.en: When choosing a business partner, trust matters most.
Doing business with family can easily lead to fights.

examples.ko: 우리는 그 동업 제안을 정중히 거절했어요.
examples.en: We politely turned down that partnership offer.

explain: '동업을 하다/시작하다/정리하다'처럼 써요. 직장에서 같이 일하는 '동료'와 달라서, 돈과 책임을 나눠서 같이 사업하는 사이를 말해요. '친구와는 동업하지 마라'는 말을 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: I run a business together with my older brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동업'을 목적어로 두고 '하다'를 붙인 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic collocation: 동업 as the object of 하다.

phrases.en: That person is my business partner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 사업하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person you run a business with.

phrases.en: Two friends opened a restaurant as a joint business.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으로'를 붙여서 어떤 방식으로 사업을 하는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -으로, it says the business is done jointly.

explain_en: It goes with '동업을 하다', '시작하다', and '정리하다'. It differs from a coworker, '동료': partners share money and responsibility in a business. You often hear the saying '친구와는 동업하지 마라'.

en: to go to school; to arrive at school

examples.en: The children go to school at eight in the morning.
It rained today, so I went to school early.
I met a friend on the way to school.
When vacation ends, I'll go to school again.

examples.ko: 등교하고 나서 도시락을 두고 온 걸 알았어요.
examples.en: After arriving at school, I realized I had left my lunchbox.

examples.ko: 늦게 등교한 학생은 교무실에 들러야 해요.
examples.en: Students who arrive late must stop by the staff room.

explain: '학교에 가다'와 거의 같지만 학교와 학생 입장에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 반대말은 '하교하다'이고, 회사에 가는 건 '출근하다'예요. '등교 시간', '등교 길'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: The roads are crowded at school commuting time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생들이 학교에 가는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the time when students head to school.

phrases.en: I met a friend on the way to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 가는 길을 한 낱말로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a single word for the way to school.

phrases.en: I walk to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통수단을 앞에 붙여서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put the means of transport before the verb.

explain_en: Going to school in the morning, one trip (등교 시간) It means almost the same as '학교에 가다' but is a more formal word from the standpoint of schools and students. The opposite is '하교하다', and going to work is '출근하다'. It also appears in '등교 시간' (school arrival time) and '등교 길' (the way to school).

t90.ax: I met a friend on the way to school.

examples.en: I failed the exam and I am so upset.
I did not pass this interview.

examples.ko: 한 번 불합격해도 다시 도전하면 돼요.
examples.en: Even if you fail once, you can try again.
What should I do if I fail?
I comforted a friend who failed the driving test.

examples.ko: 불합격할까 봐 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep all night, afraid that I might fail.

explain: 반대말은 '합격하다'예요. 대화에서는 '시험에 떨어지다'라고도 말해요. 결과를 말할 때는 '불합격이에요'처럼 '이다'를 붙여 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: I failed the driving test, so I took it again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불합격하다와 같은 뜻이지만 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 불합격하다, but more natural in conversation.

phrases.en: I checked the result, and it says I failed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 말할 때 '이다'를 붙여 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to state a result by adding '이다'.

phrases.en: I cried a lot when I heard the news that I failed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합격하지 못했다는 소식이에요. '합격 소식'의 반대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: News that you did not pass; the opposite of '합격 소식'.

explain_en: Official fail result of an exam, subject is examinee (면허 시험에 불합격하다) The opposite is '합격하다'. In conversation people also say '시험에 떨어지다'. For a result you can also say '불합격이에요' with '이다'.

t90.ax: What should I do if I fail?

examples.en: I made this whole bag by hand.
Because it is handwork, it takes a long time.

examples.ko: 기계 대신 수작업을 하는 가게가 많아요.
examples.en: Many shops do handwork instead of using machines.
Handmade soap smells really good.
Since the pottery is handmade, each piece differs a little in shape.

examples.ko: 요즘은 수작업보다 기계로 하는 일이 더 많아요.
examples.en: These days more work is done by machine than by hand.

explain: 기계로 하는 일과 짝이 되는 말이에요. 서류를 사람이 하나씩 고칠 때도 쓰고, '수작업 비누'처럼 상품 앞에 붙이면 정성을 들인 물건이라는 느낌이 나요. 보통 '수작업으로 하다/만들다'처럼 '-으로'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: This shop sells only handmade products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품 앞에 붙여 정성을 들여 만든 물건이라는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a product, it gives the feel of something made with care.

phrases.example: 기계가 고장 나서 오늘은 수작업을 했어요.
phrases.en: The machine broke down, so we did the work by hand today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계 없이 사람 손으로 일하는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when people work by hand without a machine.

phrases.en: It is a doll my grandmother made by hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수작업'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is an easier and more everyday way to say the same thing.

explain_en: Doing something by hand instead of machine (수작업으로) It pairs with work done by machines. You can use it when people fix documents one by one, and in front of a product, as in '수작업 비누', it suggests a carefully made item. It is usually used with '-으로', as in '수작업으로 하다/만들다'.

examples.ko: 아버지는 작년에 회사가 문을 닫아서 실직했어요.
examples.en: My father lost his job last year when the company closed.

examples.ko: 실직하면 한동안 실업 급여를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lose your job, you can receive unemployment benefits for a while.
I suddenly lost my job and feel lost.
I introduced a job to my friend who lost his job.
Many people worry about losing their jobs.
After losing my job, I started studying again.

explain: '실직하다'는 일자리를 잃었다는 사실을 말해요. 회사가 그만두라고 한 경우는 '해고되다', 스스로 그만두면 '퇴직하다', '사직하다'라고 해요. 그래서 실직은 이유보다 결과에 초점이 있어요.

phrases.en: The company was struggling, so I lost my job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier expression for everyday conversation.

phrases.en: There is training for people who are out of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실직하다'를 '-ㄴ'으로 바꿔 사람을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Change 실직하다 to the -ㄴ form to describe a person.

phrases.en: I lost my job, so I'm at home these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 '-해서'로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -해서 to give a reason.

explain_en: 실직하다 states the fact of having lost a job. If the company dismisses you it is 해고되다, and if you leave on your own it is 퇴직하다 or 사직하다. So 실직하다 focuses on the result rather than the reason.

en: to suffer hardships; to have a hard time

examples.en: I had a hard time finding the way.

examples.ko: 아이가 말을 안 들어서 요즘 애먹고 있어요.
examples.en: My child won't listen, so I'm having a hard time these days.

examples.ko: 컴퓨터가 고장 나서 한참 동안 애먹었던 적이 있어요.
examples.en: There was a time I struggled for ages because my computer broke.
Didn't you have a really hard time moving?
I'm struggling a lot while learning a new job.

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 며칠 애먹고 이제 괜찮아요.
examples.en: I suffered with a cold for a few days, but I'm fine now.

explain: 일이 뜻대로 안 돼서 힘들거나 고생하는 상황에 써요. 보통 '-느라 애먹다', '-면서 애먹다'처럼 원인과 같이 말해요. 비슷한 '고생하다'보다 말하기에서 더 가볍게 써요. 노력한다는 뜻의 '애를 쓰다'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I had a hard time doing my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족에게 말하는 편한 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form used with friends and family.

phrases.example: 이제는 길을 찾을 때 애먹지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't have a hard time finding my way anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들지 않게 되었다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying it is no longer difficult.

phrases.en: My computer broke down and I had a lot of trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: '많이'를 붙이면 힘든 정도가 더 크게 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 많이 makes the difficulty sound bigger.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a lot of trouble

explain_en: Intransitive — you are the one struggling with something. It is used when things don't go your way and you struggle or have a hard time. It is usually paired with the cause, as in '-느라 애먹다' or '-면서 애먹다'. It sounds lighter in speech than the similar '고생하다'. It is different from '애를 쓰다', which means to make an effort.

examples.en: I stopped by the supermarket on my way home from work.
The road home from work was jammed, so I got home late.
The subway on the way home from work is crowded.
I always walk home from work listening to music.
Thoughts of work do not leave me even on the way home.
Every evening on my way home, I stop for a moment in front of the flower shop.

explain: 반대는 '출근길'이에요. '-길'을 붙여 '그 일을 하러 가거나 마치고 돌아오는 길'을 말하는 단어가 많아요. 등굣길, 하굣길, 귀갓길도 그래요. '퇴근길에'처럼 '-에'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I bought bread on my way home from work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '퇴근길에'를 풀어서 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expanded way of saying 퇴근길에.
phrases.en_equiv: on the way home from work

phrases.en: The subway is crowded when work ends for the day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝나고 집에 가는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The time when people finish work and head home.

phrases.en: The subway on the way home from work has many people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '퇴근길'을 명사 앞에 붙여서 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 퇴근길 can be placed before a noun.

explain_en: On the way home from work (퇴근길에 장을 보다) The opposite is '출근길'. Adding '-길' makes many words for the way to or from doing something, such as '등굣길', '하굣길' and '귀갓길'. It is used with '-에', as in '퇴근길에'.

examples.en: It's bitterly cold this morning, so I layered up.
The cold snap continued and the water pipes froze.
People lined up even in the bitter cold.
My hands froze stiff in the bitter cold.
The cold snap will ease from tomorrow.
I brought hand warmers to beat the bitter cold.

explain: 눈은 안 오는데 매섭게 추운 날씨를 말할 때 주로 써요. 뉴스에서 쓰는 '한파'보다 일상 말이에요. '강추위가 몰아치다', '강추위가 계속되다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I heard a bitter cold wave will hit this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매서운 추위가 갑자기 닥친다는 느낌으로 날씨 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling that fierce cold suddenly hits; common in weather talk.

phrases.en: The bitter cold continues, so I don't want to go outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추운 날이 며칠째 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the very cold weather lasts for days.

phrases.en: I heard a cold wave is coming from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강추위'와 비슷한데 뉴스나 일기예보에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 강추위 but more typical of news and weather forecasts.

explain_en: Very harsh cold in the middle of winter (강추위가 이어지다) It is mainly used for weather that is fiercely cold without snow. It is more of an everyday word than the news term '한파'. Common phrases include '강추위가 몰아치다' and '강추위가 계속되다'.

examples.en: Mist rose over the lake in the morning.
I walked slowly along the misty riverside.
The mountain wrapped in mist looked mysterious.
The water mist soon disappears when the sun rises.
Photographers come at dawn to photograph the mist.
I remember his face faintly, like mist.

explain: 강이나 호수, 바다 위에 피어오르는 안개를 말해요. 그냥 '안개'보다 물가의 새벽 풍경이 떠오르는 말이고, 글이나 여행 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Mist rises over the river at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물 위에 안개가 천천히 올라오는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes mist slowly rising from the water.

phrases.en: Mist hung over the lake, and it was very mysterious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안개가 가득 덮인 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a place covered with mist.

phrases.example: 짙은 물안개 때문에 앞이 잘 안 보였어요.
phrases.en: Because of the thick mist, I couldn't see well ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안개가 많을 때 앞에 '짙은'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '짙은' before it when the mist is heavy.

explain_en: It means fog rising over a river, lake or sea. Compared with plain '안개', it brings to mind a dawn scene by the water and often appears in writing and travel stories.

examples.en: A cold north wind blows in winter.
The north wind is blowing hard and my hands are freezing.
I walked to school facing the north wind.

examples.ko: 오늘은 북풍 때문에 체감 온도가 더 낮아요.
examples.en: Because of the north wind, it feels colder today.

examples.ko: 북풍이 부는 날에는 목도리를 꼭 해요.
examples.en: I always wear a scarf on days when the north wind blows.
A north wind suddenly gusted and the windows rattled.

explain: 북쪽에서 불어오는 바람이에요. 한국에서는 겨울의 차갑고 센 바람을 떠올리게 해요. 반대로 남쪽에서 불어오는 바람은 '남풍'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 찬 북풍이 불어서 두꺼운 옷을 입었어요.
phrases.en: A cold north wind was blowing, so I wore thick clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울 바람을 말할 때 '찬'과 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 찬 when talking about winter wind.

phrases.en: I walked into the north wind and my face felt frozen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 몸에 직접 닿을 때 '맞다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 맞다 when the wind hits your body directly.

phrases.en: A warm south wind blows in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '북풍'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 북풍.

explain_en: Cold wind from the north, common in winter. It is the wind that blows from the north. In Korea it brings to mind the cold, strong winds of winter. The wind from the south is called '남풍'.

examples.en: Bedbugs showed up at the hotel, so I changed rooms.
If bedbugs bite you, it itches a lot all night.

examples.ko: 빈대는 낮에 침대 틈에 숨어 있다가 밤에 나와요.
examples.en: Bedbugs hide in bed cracks during the day and come out at night.

examples.ko: 이불을 뜨거운 물로 빨면 빈대를 없애는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Washing bedding in hot water helps get rid of bedbugs.

examples.ko: 집에 바퀴벌레도 있고 빈대도 나와서 이사했어요.
examples.en: There were cockroaches and bedbugs in the house, so I moved.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 빈대 소식을 보고 침대 밑을 확인했어요.
examples.en: After seeing news about bedbugs, I checked under my bed.

explain: 사람의 피를 빠는 작은 벌레예요. 남에게 붙어서 공짜로 얻어먹는 사람을 놀릴 때도 '빈대'라고 하고, '빈대떡'은 음식 이름이라서 벌레와 관계없이 따로 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: I mooched off a friend and got a free lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 기대어 공짜로 얻어먹거나 신세를 지는 것을 가볍게 말해요. 친한 사이에서 농담처럼 쓰는 구어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lightly describes leaning on others to get free meals or favors. It is casual talk, often used jokingly between close friends.

explain_en: It is a small insect that sucks human blood. People also call someone who freeloads off others a '빈대', and '빈대떡' is a food name, so learn it separately from the bug.

examples.en: Hot steam comes out of the kettle.

examples.ko: 욕실에 증기가 가득 차서 거울이 흐려졌어요.
examples.en: The bathroom filled with steam and the mirror fogged up.
In the old days, steam locomotives pulled the trains.
The dumplings cooked in steam are soft.

examples.ko: 다리미에서 증기가 나오면 옷이 잘 펴져요.
examples.en: When steam comes out of the iron, clothes smooth out well.
Be careful with the steam so you do not get burned.

explain: 일상에서는 '김'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. '밥에서 김이 나요'처럼요. '증기'는 '증기 기관', '증기 다리미'처럼 기계나 과학 이야기에서 주로 써요.

phrases.en: Steam is coming off the hot soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 물에서 나오는 증기는 일상에서 '김'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, steam from food or water is called '김'.

phrases.example: 증기 기관이 생기면서 기차가 달리기 시작했어요.
phrases.en: Trains began to run once the steam engine was invented.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학이나 역사 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in talks about science or history.

phrases.en: I steam the dumplings and eat them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 증기로 음식을 익히는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way of cooking food with hot steam.

explain_en: In daily life Koreans more often say '김', as in '밥에서 김이 나요'. '증기' shows up mainly in talk about machines and science, such as '증기 기관' and '증기 다리미'.

t90.ax: Hot steam comes out of the kettle.

examples.en: This winter is terribly cold.
That friend is extremely stubborn.
That person grew up in dire poverty.

examples.ko: 어제 먹은 음식이 지독히 매워서 혼났어요.
examples.en: The food I ate yesterday was awfully spicy and I had a hard time.
That night it rained terribly hard.
It was an unbearably lonely night.

explain: 좋지 않은 정도가 심할 때 써서 추위, 가난, 외로움 같은 부정적인 말과 잘 어울려요. '지독히도'처럼 '도'를 붙이면 더 강조돼요. 형용사는 '지독하다'예요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 어릴 때 지독히 가난했어요.
phrases.en: He was terribly poor as a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가난처럼 힘든 상황이 아주 심하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a hard situation like poverty is extreme.

phrases.en: The nights alone are terribly lonely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도'를 붙이면 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 도 makes the feeling stronger.

phrases.en: My younger sibling absolutely hates bugs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싫어하는 마음이 아주 크다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows a very strong dislike.

explain_en: Intensely, usually for negative things (지독히 미워하다) It is used when something bad is extreme, so it goes with negative words like cold, poverty or loneliness. Adding '도', as in '지독히도', adds emphasis. The adjective is '지독하다'.

examples.ko: 만두를 찜통에 넣고 십 분만 쪄요.
examples.en: Put the dumplings in the steamer and steam them for ten minutes.
Steam is rising from the steamer.

examples.ko: 찜통이 너무 작아서 한 번에 다 못 쪄요.
examples.en: The steamer is too small to steam everything at once.
If there's no water at the bottom of the steamer, it will burn.

examples.ko: 새 찜통을 사서 고구마를 쪄 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought a new steamer and steamed sweet potatoes.

examples.ko: 오늘은 밖에 나가면 찜통 속에 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Going outside today feels like being inside a steamer.

explain: 음식을 찌는 큰 통이에요. 날씨 이야기에서는 푹푹 찌는 더위의 비유로도 많이 나와요. 짝말로 '찜통에 찌다', '찜통에 넣다'를 써요.

phrases.en: This summer the sweltering heat lasted a whole month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찜통 속처럼 습하고 푹푹 찌는 더위를 말해요. 뉴스와 일상에서 모두 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means muggy, steaming heat as if you were inside a steamer. It is used in both the news and daily talk.

explain_en: It is a large pot for steaming food. In weather talk it often appears as a metaphor for oppressive, humid heat. Common pairings are '찜통에 찌다' and '찜통에 넣다'.
